To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new air Cherenov counter concept for the study of cosmic rays.

we have built and operated a prototype array of air Cherenkov detectors, and that we are presently building a large array of Cherenkov counters, which will be used in combination with the ground level scinitillation counter array of the HEGRA experiment.
the proposed Cherenkov array will be able to detect the diffuse γ radiation coming predominantly from the direction of the galactic plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new techniques in order to detect and identify the highest-energy cosmic rays and γ rays.
the development and construction of an array of air Cherenkov detectors for the detection of extended air showers of primary energies > 5 10 13 eV and of zenith angle up to 35 degrees.

the study of the diffuse galactic γ radiation, the study of γ/hadron separation, the study of cosmic ray energy spectrum up to 10 17 meV, the study of the cosmic ray composition, the search for point sources of cosmic rays and the search for new physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new Cherenkov array is expected to provide a unique and powerful tool for the study of the VHE and U HE cosmic radiation.
the HEGRA experiment is one of the most successful and most productive VHE γ-ray observatories worldwide.
the new air Cherenko counter array is an important and essential part of the planned upgrade of the HEGRA array.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are building a new air Cherenkow counter array for a new experiment on La Palma, Canary Islands.
the proposed air Cherenkov array is a powerful tool in the study of cosmic ray physics in the energy range 5 × 1012 – 5 × 1020 meV.
the new array will be a powerful instrument for the study of the diffuse γ ray background and for the search for γ ray point sources in the TeV range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of Cherenkov and scintillation counters is a very promising tool for the study of the diffuse γ-ray background.
a new air Cherenkow counter concept can be built with an array of angle integrators.
the proposed array will be a powerful instrument for the study of cosmic ray physics and will be able to detect the diffuse galactic γ radiation.
